title: World premiere of John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s films Two Virgins and Film No. 5 | 1968
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s films Two Virgins and Film No. 5 had their world premiere on 14 November 1968.

The screenings were at the fourth Chicago International Film Festival, at the Playboy Theater at 1204 North Dearborn Street.

Both films were made on 9 June 1968 in the garden of Kenwood, Lennon’s home in Weybridge, England, on 9 June 1968. They were created by a four-man crew led by William Wareing.

They filmed Lennon in the garden’s outdoor pool area, smiling into the lens for just under three minutes. It was shot using a high-speed 16mm camera which allowed slow-motion capture.

The 51-minute Film No 5, also known as Smile, contained this footage. A soundtrack of birds and aeroplanes can be heard in realtime.

The 19-minute Two Virgins used a camera running at normal speed. The crew first filmed Lennon’s face looking into the camera. They then rewound the film reel and filmed Ono doing the same. The double-exposure created a superimposed effect of the two faces. The couple were also filmed hugging and kissing.

The screening took place at midnight, with all tickets for the theatre’s 606 seats sold out. Attendees brought musical instruments as per Lennon’s instruction to make their own noise for the soundtrack.
